title: Career Roadmap— B.Sc. Physiotherapy-Related Basic Sciences → Lab Demonstrator
summary: A Lab Demonstrator supports practical teaching in educational institutions by preparing laboratory sessions, demonstrating scientific procedures, helping students use equipment correctly, and maintaining a safe, organized learning environment.

blocks.text: A Lab Demonstrator supports practical teaching in educational institutions by preparing laboratory sessions, demonstrating scientific procedures, helping students use equipment correctly, and maintaining a safe, organized learning environment.

For a graduate in physiotherapy-related basic sciences, potential workplaces include physiotherapy colleges, allied health science institutions, anatomy and physiology teaching laboratories, and universities. The precise eligibility depends on the subject taught and the institution's recruitment rules.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: A B.Sc. in a related basic science may qualify someone for some laboratory-support roles, but it does not automatically qualify them to teach every physiotherapy subject. Roles involving clinical instruction or professional physiotherapy practice may require a recognized physiotherapy qualification, registration where applicable, and additional experience.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Prepare laboratory equipment, models, specimens, and teaching materials.
Demonstrate approved practical procedures and explain basic concepts.
Assist students with laboratory exercises and measurements.
Maintain equipment inventories, logs, and practical records.
Follow institutional hygiene, biosafety, and waste-disposal procedures.
Report damaged equipment, safety issues, or incidents to the responsible faculty member.

blocks.text: Work settings
Universities, physiotherapy colleges, allied health institutes, teaching labs
Core strengths
Scientific knowledge, communication, organization, safety awareness
Entry-level titles
Lab Demonstrator, Practical Lab Assistant, Laboratory Instructor Trainee
Career directions
Laboratory coordination, teaching support, research assistance, postgraduate study
The phrase “physiotherapy-related basic sciences” can cover different degree subjects. Choose roles that match the actual degree and transcript.
1. Anatomy Laboratory
Assist with anatomical models, skeletal specimens, charts, and approved practical demonstrations. Learn anatomical terminology, specimen handling rules, and institutional safety protocols.
2. Physiology Laboratory
Support practicals on physiological measurements, reflexes, exercise responses, and basic human-body functions using approved equipment and supervision.
3. Biomechanics and Kinesiology Laboratory
Help students understand joint movements, posture, levers, gait concepts, and measurement tools such as goniometers, where appropriate to the programme.
4. Physiotherapy Practical Laboratory

Assist with equipment preparation and practical-class logistics. Clinical techniques and therapeutic equipment demonstrations should be undertaken only when permitted by the role, qualifications, and supervising faculty.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Target anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, or general laboratory-support positions that explicitly accept your B.Sc. subject. Avoid assuming that a basic-science degree qualifies you for clinical teaching duties.
This is a suggested three-year preparation plan, not a prescribed curriculum for every B.Sc. programme. Adapt it to the actual degree, subject specialization, and laboratory facilities available.
Year 1
Foundations
Build subject knowledge and laboratory discipline

items.text: Study the relevant fundamentals of human anatomy, physiology, biology, or biomechanics.
Learn laboratory equipment names, functions, cleaning, storage, and basic maintenance.
Practise measurement recording, unit conversion, calculations, and accurate labelling.
Learn scientific terminology and how to explain concepts in simple language.
Understand hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), and laboratory safety.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Prepare a set of practical notes explaining the purpose, equipment, procedure, precautions, and expected observations for five relevant experiments.
Year 2
Practical skills
Learn to assist with practical classes

items.text: Practise demonstrations under faculty supervision.
Learn to prepare equipment and materials before scheduled practicals.
Record observations, maintain inventory registers, and identify equipment faults.
Develop Excel skills for recording results and preparing charts.
Practise explaining practical steps, answering student questions, and reporting errors.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Create a practical-laboratory manual for one subject and demonstrate selected procedures under supervision.
Year 3
Job readiness
Prepare for educational and research settings

items.text: Complete a supervised laboratory project or practical teaching placement, where available.
Develop demonstration plans and student-friendly practical worksheets.
Learn stock management, calibration records, equipment maintenance logs, and incident reporting.
Prepare a CV highlighting the exact laboratory subjects and equipment you know.
Research eligibility criteria for demonstrator, laboratory assistant, and research assistant positions.
Investigate postgraduate study if the roles you want require a master's degree.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Present a practical manual, a sample laboratory inventory, and an example of a student-friendly demonstration plan.

blocks.text: For any work involving human participants, biological specimens, or clinical equipment, follow the institution's approved protocols and the instructions of qualified staff. A demonstrator should not perform clinical procedures independently merely because they have observed them in a teaching laboratory.
These projects can demonstrate readiness for laboratory-support work. Use simulated data or approved teaching materials; never use identifiable patient data without proper authorization.
Project 1 — Practical Demonstration Manual

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner
Create practical guides for five to ten topics from your strongest subject.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Each guide should include learning objectives, equipment, steps, precautions, expected observations, and review questions.
Project 2 — Laboratory Inventory and Maintenance Tracker

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner to intermediate
Build an Excel tracker for equipment identification, location, condition, inspection dates, maintenance due dates, and stock levels.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A sample inventory sheet, maintenance schedule, and simple dashboard using fictional laboratory data.
Project 3 — Practical Results Workbook

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate
Use instructor-provided or simulated observations to demonstrate accurate data entry, calculations, averages, charts, and interpretation.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A spreadsheet with clearly labelled units, quality checks, graphs, and a short explanation of limitations.
Project 4 — Micro-Demonstration Portfolio

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Job preparation
Prepare a short teaching demonstration on a topic from your degree, using approved models, diagrams, or equipment.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A lesson plan, a short presentation, a safety checklist, and sample questions to assess student understanding.

blocks.label: Recommended final-year project
blocks.text: Combine a practical manual with an equipment inventory and a short demonstration portfolio for one subject, such as anatomy, physiology, or biomechanics. This shows that you can support both the scientific and organizational sides of a laboratory.

Because the degree in the supplied record is described broadly as “B.Sc – Physiotherapy-related Basic Sciences,” the exact degree title matters. A B.Sc. in anatomy, physiology, biological sciences, or another basic science may be assessed differently by different employers.
Before applying, check:

items.text: The exact degree and subject specialization accepted in the job notification.
Whether the position is a laboratory demonstrator, technical assistant, tutor, or teaching faculty role.
Whether a postgraduate qualification is required or preferred.
Whether practical experience, teaching experience, or equipment-specific skills are required.
Whether the role involves clinical instruction that requires a recognized professional qualification.

Weekly job-search routine

rows.text: Contact faculty members or laboratory supervisors professionally

blocks.text: When contacting a college, share your degree title, relevant subject knowledge, laboratory experience, and the type of demonstrator role you are seeking.
There is no single certificate that qualifies every B.Sc. graduate for every demonstrator role. Prefer training that addresses a clear gap in the job requirements.

blocks.text: The titles and requirements vary by institution. A demonstrator position does not automatically lead to a faculty appointment; teaching and research posts can have separate qualification requirements.
Days 1–30
Clarify and learn
Confirm the exact degree requirements for target jobs. Revise your strongest subject, learn laboratory safety, and prepare practical notes for five topics.
Days 31–60
Build evidence
Create a practical demonstration manual, an equipment inventory tracker, and a sample results workbook. Seek supervised laboratory experience through your institution.
Days 61–90
Apply

Prepare a subject-specific CV, research college and university recruitment notices, and apply to roles whose eligibility criteria match your qualifications. Practise explaining a practical procedure clearly and safely.
Lab demonstrator readiness
I know the exact degree requirements for my target positions.
I can explain core concepts from my relevant basic-science subject.
I understand laboratory safety and equipment-handling procedures.
I can prepare a practical guide and explain an experiment clearly.
I can maintain inventory, maintenance, and results records.
I have completed a practical project or supervised laboratory experience.
I have a targeted CV and have identified suitable vacancies.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Start by targeting laboratory demonstrator and laboratory assistant roles that explicitly accept your B.Sc. subject. Develop strong practical knowledge, safe equipment handling, clear teaching demonstrations, and accurate recordkeeping. If your long-term goal is to teach physiotherapy-specific clinical subjects, check the required professional qualification and postgraduate pathway before choosing your next step.
